ballot_rationales.rationale: The exclusivity is bounded to Analyzed Work and prevents downstream artifacts from becoming competing operational authorities while preserving an explicit blocked return path for changed decisions.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: The engineering-change-analysis implementation-preparation contract governs construction of the current Engineering Brief for Analyzed Work.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Retain the explicit Main-to-analysis update and redispatch path when the Brief is insufficient or a protected decision changes.

ballot_rationales.rationale: A single current Brief prevents competing operational interpretations and keeps acceptance, ownership, rollback, and the executable slice auditable. If analysis input changes, the safe response is a revised current Brief, not an untracked parallel authority.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies only to Analyzed Work after engineering-change-analysis has produced the current Engineering Brief; underlying requests, source, tests, and specialist evidence remain inputs to that analysis.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Keep requests and new evidence routed through renewed analysis; do not execute from a competing authority.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The sole-authority statement is explicitly limited to Analyzed Work and the implementation-preparation mode contract, preventing derived artifacts from competing with the accepted Brief.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies only while engineering-change-analysis produces or updates the current Engineering Brief for Analyzed Work.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Retain the Analyzed Work and mode-contract bounds and route protected-decision changes back through Brief revision.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Treating these materials as inputs preserves their evidentiary force without allowing an unincorporated source or specialist result to silently mutate the executable analysis contract.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: The rule applies only inside the Engineering Brief template after source and specialist evidence has been incorporated by analysis.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Route any new user decision or conflicting evidence back through Main for an updated Brief before further dispatch.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The statement classifies evidence and requests as inputs rather than executable authority. That boundary preserves traceability while still allowing contradicting evidence or failures to reopen analysis and produce an updated Brief.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies within the Engineering Brief contract: listed materials inform analysis, but operational acceptance and task authority come from the current Brief produced from them.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Preserve evidence provenance and regenerate the current Brief when inputs materially change.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The template correctly classifies requests, source, tests, external evidence, and Specialist results as inputs rather than parallel operational analysis authorities.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies within the Engineering Brief template after source and Specialist evidence are incorporated into the current Brief.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Keep the input-versus-authority distinction adjacent to the incorporation rule and Brief update path.

ballot_rationales.rationale: A single current Brief provides deterministic authority for analyzed execution and prevents derived DAG, task, implementation, or review artifacts from creating split-brain decisions.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: The exclusivity is expressly limited to operational analysis authority for Analyzed Work and its named authoritative Brief sections.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Keep protected-decision conflicts fail closed and require analysis to issue an updated Brief followed by affected-task redispatch.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The template needs one authoritative state for acceptance, invariants, placement, rollback, and the first slice. Competing documents would make negative outcomes and completion evidence indeterminate; updates belong in a newly current Brief.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Scoped expressly to Analyzed Work and to the current Engineering Brief; evidence may trigger re-analysis but does not directly supersede the Brief.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Fail closed on a missing or stale Brief and route changed facts back through analysis.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The statement is bounded by Analyzed Work and establishes one operational Brief authority, avoiding contradictory downstream acceptance, ownership, and placement decisions.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies to the current Engineering Brief produced for the active Analyzed Work lineage.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Preserve the Analyzed Work qualifier and require Brief regeneration when protected decisions legitimately change.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Verbatim dispatch and prohibition on DAG reselection preserve the analyst-owned safe first slice, preventing control or planning layers from altering acceptance and execution scope without evidence.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: The current Engineering Brief has already selected a complete Task Contract v2 First Executable Slice for Analyzed Work.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: When dispatch cannot honor the slice or the DAG conflicts, block and return through Main for Brief revision rather than reinterpret locally.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Verbatim dispatch and non-reselection preserve the analyzed slice binding and prevent silent semantic drift between analysis, planning, and execution. A discovered incompatibility must be surfaced for renewed analysis rather than locally reinterpreted.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies after the current Brief fixes its First Executable Slice; Main and the DAG planner may report a blocker or request renewed analysis but may not silently change that slice.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: On an unexecutable slice, report the blocker and obtain a freshly authorized Brief instead of reselection.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Verbatim dispatch and prohibition on reselection preserve the analysis-owned First Executable Slice across Main and DAG projection boundaries.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies after the Engineering Brief has selected a complete and safe First Executable Slice.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Keep conflicts on slice content routed to an updated Brief and redispatch rather than downstream reinterpretation.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Derived artifacts may project execution and evidence but cannot safely redefine protected analysis decisions, because doing so would bypass ownership, acceptance, rollback, and compatibility reasoning.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: The rule governs artifacts derived from the current Engineering Brief for Analyzed Work and names the protected decision set explicitly.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: A required protected-decision change must block the artifact and return to analysis for a new Brief and targeted redispatch.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The listed artifacts are downstream execution and evidence records. Prohibiting them from redefining governing fields prevents scope, ownership, compatibility, and rollback from changing without analysis and keeps failures attributable to one contract.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies to artifacts derived from the current Engineering Brief; legitimate changes to any listed governing field require renewed analysis and a replacement current Brief.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Reject downstream redefinition and reopen analysis whenever a governing field must change.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The protected-field list correctly constrains derived artifacts from silently becoming competing authorities for accepted analysis decisions.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies to Task DAGs, Task Contracts, Implementation Handoffs, and Review Handoffs derived from a current Brief.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Retain the explicit protected fields and return any required decision change through analysis for Brief revision.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Main is dispatch-only, so regenerating or reinterpreting an analysis-selected Task Contract would exceed its authority and could silently change scope, validation, ownership, or rollback obligations.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: The implementation-preparation mode has produced a current Engineering Brief containing a complete First Executable Slice.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: If verbatim dispatch is impossible or unsafe, Main must return the conflict to analysis instead of adapting the slice.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Main is a dispatcher, so regenerating or reinterpreting the analyzed contract would create unaudited acceptance and failure semantics. Blocking and returning to analysis is the safe boundary when the Brief cannot be executed as written.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies to dispatch of the current Engineering Brief and its First Executable Slice; changed facts are handled by renewed analysis, not by Main rewriting the contract.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Require verbatim dispatch and send changed conditions back to the analysis owner.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Main's prohibition on regeneration or reinterpretation preserves the exact analysis-selected slice and prevents dispatch-layer semantic drift.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies when Main dispatches the First Executable Slice selected in the current Engineering Brief.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Maintain verbatim dispatch and use the defined blocked-to-analysis path when the slice cannot be executed safely.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The DAG is explicitly a projection, so forbidding it from selecting the first slice or altering protected Brief decisions preserves dependency planning without granting parallel analysis authority.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: The task DAG contract applies only after a current Engineering Brief exists and already owns the First Executable Slice.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Block a conflicting projection and return through Main to analysis for an updated Brief and redispatch.

ballot_rationales.rationale: A DAG represents dependencies among accepted tasks; allowing it to replace the selected slice or alter governing contract fields would turn a scheduling artifact into a second analysis authority and make completion evidence ambiguous.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies to Task DAG derivation from an accepted Brief; the planner may expose blocking dependencies but changes to the slice or governing fields require renewed analysis.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Keep DAG output dependency-only and reopen analysis for any change to the selected slice or contract.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The Task DAG is a projection surface, so forbidding slice reselection and protected-decision modification preserves correct analysis ownership.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies only to a Task DAG derived from an accepted current Engineering Brief for Analyzed Work.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Keep DAG authority limited to task decomposition, dependencies, scheduling, and integration ownership.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Specialists contribute bounded evidence and decisions for incorporation, but parallel authority would make ownership and conflict resolution ambiguous and permit untracked changes to protected Brief decisions.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Within Analyzed Work, analysis owns the current Brief and incorporates a specialist result before that result can affect implementation.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Preserve specialist scope and rationale in the Brief, and route any unresolved structural conflict back to analysis before dispatch.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Specialists contribute bounded evidence and professional-risk judgments, but parallel operational authority would permit conflicting acceptance or rollback decisions. Their findings must be incorporated through the accountable analysis path.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies to Specialist participation in Analyzed Work: specialist input remains evidence until the analysis owner incorporates it into the current Brief.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Route material Specialist findings into a revised Brief before they affect operational work.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Specialist evidence may inform placement or risk decisions, but the Brief must incorporate it before it gains operational effect.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies to Specialists invoked for unresolved structural choices during Engineering Brief preparation.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Retain explicit incorporation into the current Brief before Specialist conclusions affect implementation.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The word only limits the impact section to material consequences rather than claiming those categories are exhaustive runtime facts, keeping the Brief decision-relevant without suppressing material transitive effects.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: This is an output-shaping rule for the Contract, Data, and Failure Impact section of an Engineering Brief.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Continue requiring direct and transitive consumers and include any material consequence that falls within the named compatibility and operational categories.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The word 'only' limits this Brief section to material impact rather than excluding required impact classes. The enumerated classes cover direct and transitive compatibility, failure, security, reliability, release, documentation, and generated-output consequences without inviting irrelevant narrative.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies specifically to the Contract / Data / Failure Impact section; materiality is required, direct and transitive consumers are included, and other Brief sections retain their own acceptance and risk responsibilities.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Retain materiality and consumer tracing; use other Brief sections for impacts outside this section's contract.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The word only limits the section to material impact categories while still requiring direct and transitive consumer coverage.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies when populating Contract, Data, and Failure Impact in an implementation-preparation Engineering Brief.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Preserve materiality as the inclusion boundary without omitting direct or transitive consumers.

ballot_rationales.rationale: A parallel analysis authority would permit divergent placement, invariant, and contract decisions, so this prohibition is necessary to retain one auditable source of operational execution truth.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: The rule is scoped to implementation-preparation and the current Engineering Brief produced for Analyzed Work.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Incorporate specialist evidence into the Brief and block downstream conflicts for analysis-owned revision and redispatch.

ballot_rationales.rationale: One analysis authority is necessary for deterministic acceptance, boundaries, and failure handling. Independent evidence and review remain valid, but creating a competing operational analysis record would break provenance and leave no reliable completion contract.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies to implementation-preparation for Analyzed Work; new facts must update or replace the current Brief through analysis rather than creating a parallel authority.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Consolidate changed analysis into one replacement current Brief and reject parallel operational records.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Prohibiting a parallel analysis authority prevents Specialists and derived artifacts from producing incompatible implementation decisions outside the current Brief.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies during implementation-preparation after source evidence and any Specialist result are reconciled into the Brief.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Keep one Brief authority and route legitimate decision changes through explicit Brief update and redispatch.

ballot_rationales.rationale: An implementation handoff reports performed work and fresh evidence; allowing it to redefine protected analysis decisions would let the implementer expand authority after execution and invalidate review binding.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: The handoff is a derived projection for Analyzed Work after the verbatim-dispatched First Executable Slice has been executed.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Mark conflicting assignments blocked and return through Main to analysis whenever a protected decision or slice must change.

ballot_rationales.rationale: An Implementation Handoff should report execution and fresh evidence, including failures and proof limits, but cannot retroactively change the acceptance or rollback contract it claims to satisfy. That separation makes validation auditable.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies to a handoff derived from the accepted Task Contract; material contract changes require renewed analysis rather than edits in the execution report.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Treat contract drift in a handoff as a blocker and obtain renewed analysis before claiming completion.

ballot_rationales.rationale: An Implementation Handoff records execution evidence and must not overwrite the accepted decisions that authorized the implementation.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies to Implementation Handoffs for work dispatched from a current Engineering Brief First Executable Slice.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Keep the handoff evidence-only and return protected-decision conflicts to analysis before further execution.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The protected-field prohibition keeps derived artifacts subordinate to the source-backed Brief and prevents task planning, implementation, or review from silently expanding scope or changing contract semantics.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: The implementation-preparation contract defines these artifacts as derived from the current Engineering Brief for Analyzed Work.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Use the stated blocked Main-to-analysis recovery path for any downstream conflict or necessary protected-decision update.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Derived planning and handoff artifacts must preserve the accepted governing fields so evidence is evaluated against a stable contract. If a boundary, invariant, or rollback rule is wrong, renewed analysis is required instead of downstream redefinition.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies to artifacts derived from the current Engineering Brief; they may add execution detail and evidence without changing the listed authoritative semantics.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Compare derived artifacts to the current Brief and reopen analysis for any semantic change.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The rule correctly protects Brief-owned acceptance, ownership, placement, contract, rollback, and slice decisions from downstream derived artifacts.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies to all Task DAGs, Task Contracts, Implementation Handoffs, and Review Handoffs derived from the current Brief.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Maintain the enumerated protected boundaries and use Brief revision for any authorized change.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Review must not silently change its own governing risk level; self-upgrade would bypass Brief authority, historical level binding, required gates, and the Main-mediated recomputation path.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: The rule applies during implementation review when a newly discovered L4 or L5 risk may invalidate the assigned Effective Level.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Return the new risk blocked through Main for Brief update, level recomputation, and correctly scoped redispatch.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Effective Level is an externally bound review contract, so self-upgrade would invalidate the assignment and its evidence binding. Newly discovered risk should be reported as a finding or authority mismatch and routed for a fresh authorized review, not silently absorbed.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies during independent review under an assigned Effective Level; the reviewer may identify that stronger review is required but cannot alter the binding itself.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Report newly discovered risk and request fresh authority rather than changing Effective Level in place.

ballot_rationales.rationale: A review agent cannot change its own assigned Effective Level because that would bypass the analysis and dispatch authority boundary.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies during implementation review when new risk evidence may invalidate the assigned Effective Level.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Keep self-upgrade forbidden and return newly discovered L4 or L5 risk through Main for recomputation.

ballot_rationales.rationale: L4 requires one accountable independent final implementation review while adding only evidence-triggered gates or specialists; an automatic extra reviewer would add count without addressing a named risk.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: The current task has Effective Level L4 under the public execution-level contract and retains one primary final review owner.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Trigger additional gates, specialists, or design-carried pre-review only for concrete risks and keep final review coverage complete.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The count defines one independent final implementation review as the common assurance anchor; L4 adds every triggered gate and specialist rather than treating one reviewer as sufficient for all risks. Blocking findings still require repair, fresh validation, and fresh review.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies only when Effective Level is L4 and the trigger matrix independently determines all additional gates and specialists; it is not a cap on risk-triggered review.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Enforce all triggered gates and require fresh validation plus re-review after any repair.

ballot_rationales.rationale: L4 retains one independent final implementation review while adding only risk-triggered gates, Specialists, or design-carried pre-review evidence.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies when the authoritative execution-level contract sets Effective Level L4 for the implementation review.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Retain the base review and require every triggered specialist dimension without treating L4 as an automatic reviewer count.

ballot_rationales.rationale: L3's single independent final review supplies accountable full-scope coverage, while risk-triggered just-in-time lenses add expertise only where a concrete boundary warrants it.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: The current implementation task has Effective Level L3 and no separately triggered higher-risk gate requiring additional independent evidence.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Add a named JIT lens when concrete security, contract, architecture, data, or reliability risk is actually triggered.

ballot_rationales.rationale: For L3, one independent final implementation review supplies the complete base decision while risk-triggered lenses add domain depth. This avoids duplicate generic review without suppressing negative, boundary, security, or reliability examination when triggered.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies only to L3 under the defined base matrix and JIT trigger rules; each triggered professional-risk dimension remains mandatory and cannot be omitted by the fixed final-review count.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Apply every triggered JIT lens and preserve the full base-matrix verdict and residual-risk record.

ballot_rationales.rationale: L3 preserves the full independent base review and adds JIT lenses only when concrete risk triggers make them relevant.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies when the authoritative execution-level contract sets Effective Level L3 for the current implementation review.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Keep all base review dimensions mandatory and add rather than substitute any risk-triggered JIT lens.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Resolving the actual diff, every changed file, and reachable consumers is the minimum review surface needed to avoid approving a local line while missing the consequential regression path.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: The code-review capability is active for a bounded implementation or repair review with an actual latest diff.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Fail closed when the diff, changed-file set, or consequential caller and configuration surface cannot be established.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Review claims cannot be complete without resolving the latest actual diff and every changed file within the task boundary. The universal scope is necessary to catch split-file regressions, misplaced ownership, and unreviewed generated or contract changes.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies to implementation or repair review after the Current Task Boundary and latest diff are resolved; inaccessible diff scope must be marked unverified rather than treated as reviewed.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Block the verdict when the latest actual diff or any changed file cannot be inspected.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Resolving the task boundary, latest diff, every changed file, and reachable impact is the necessary first action for any bounded code review.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies whenever the code-review capability is selected for a task-local implementation or repair review.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Keep this front-loaded root rule and stop approval when any part of the review surface remains unresolved.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Treating absent or unknown host mode as unsupported is a fail-closed capability boundary that prevents Main from inventing diff or validation access and issuing an ungrounded review claim.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: The dispatch-only Main control prompt must select behavior from declared host capability rather than infer unavailable tooling.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Use the no-edit utility comparison when explicitly supported; otherwise block review or closure and mark the relevant scope unverified.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Capability must come from declared profile authority, not inference from task wording or apparent tool access. This prevents unauthorized mutation and makes no-edit utility work deterministic; an absent capability is a routing or authority blocker.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies to control-plane profile selection and dispatch; the referenced utility_no_edit capsule supplies the declared non-modifying path instead of inferred capability.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Fail closed on absent profile authority and use only the declared no-edit utility route.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The control plane must not assume unavailable host capabilities because unsupported diff or validation modes require fail-closed routing.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies when host diff, validation, or utility no-edit capability is absent or unrecognized during Direct Task routing.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Keep capability inference prohibited and use the named utility no-edit capsule or unsupported-mode blocker.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The detected span is a compact dispatch control contract, not tutorial exposition; its clauses encode distinct authority, scheduling, evidence, recovery, and closure rules for runtime routing.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Main is a dispatch-only control prompt whose terse operational clauses are consumed as routing policy rather than learner-facing explanatory content.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Keep semantic and readability adjudication separate, preserve the explicit section boundaries, and continue generated control-prompt validation.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The detected span is compact operational control syntax defining Brief authority, verbatim slice dispatch, and specialist-input activation. Its marker density is caused by repeated routing conditions and prohibitions, not by tutorial examples or explanatory teaching content, so this detector family does not apply.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: The detector's tutorial-density family is inapplicable because the bound span is an operational routing contract, not teaching or example content.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Retain the source and record this candidate-bound false-positive; re-review if the span or detector evidence changes.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The flagged span is compact control-plane policy for authority, scheduling, review evidence, and closure states, not tutorial or explanatory teaching content.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: The detector applies only when root text teaches through examples or extended explanation rather than defining executable control contracts.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Retain the operational clauses and treat syntax markers, state values, and routing arrows as contract notation rather than tutorial signals.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Focused evidence must exercise the changed behavior and consequential negative outcome that could realize the failure; broad green status cannot prove an untested mechanism absent.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: The code-review capability is assessing evidence for a bounded changed mechanism and its reachable negative and boundary outcomes.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Name unexercised risk as a proof limit and require targeted validation rather than accepting aggregate coverage or unrelated passing tests.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Evidence must address the actual failure mechanism and consequential negative outcomes; adjacent success cannot establish recurrence prevention. Focused proof also exposes when an environment or boundary remains unverified instead of overstating validation.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies after the review surface and failure mechanism are identified; the required evidence may be test, inspection, or other proportionate proof, but its limits must remain explicit.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Name missing trigger coverage and residual risk; do not treat adjacent passing behavior as proof.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Focused proof must exercise the changed failure mechanism and consequential negative outcomes; broad green status cannot close an untested risk.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies when code-review evaluates validation evidence for changed behavior and reachable failure outcomes.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Keep the rule in the root review sequence and state proof limits whenever focused mechanism evidence is unavailable.

ballot_rationales.rationale: L1 and L2 still require one independent final implementation review covering the base matrix; lower execution level narrows added depth but does not remove core correctness dimensions.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: The current implementation task has Effective Level L1 or L2 and no risk-triggered specialist boundary beyond the base matrix.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Apply the complete base matrix and route any newly discovered level-invalidating risk through Main instead of self-upgrading.

ballot_rationales.rationale: One independent final review is the explicit assurance mechanism for L1-L2 and must still decide the full base matrix, including boundaries, failures, validation freshness, ownership, scope, and residual risk. A fixed reviewer count does not reduce those dimensions.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies only to work authoritatively bound to Effective Level L1 or L2 and to the complete base review matrix; a discovered binding inconsistency must be surfaced rather than ignored.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Require the complete base matrix and route any authority inconsistency for a fresh binding.

ballot_rationales.rationale: L1 and L2 still receive one independent final review covering the complete base matrix, so lower level does not remove Core dimensions.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies when the authoritative execution-level contract sets Effective Level L1 or L2 for implementation review.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Retain the complete base matrix and do not treat the level as permission to omit any Core review dimension.

ballot_rationales.rationale: A regression guard has evidentiary value only when it reproduces the causal trigger and observes the matching failure mechanism, not merely adjacent behavior that was already correct.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: The regression-testing capability is invoked only for an accepted prior defect, incident, finding, or equivalent known recurrence mechanism.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: When direct red proof is unsafe or inadmissible, document the proof limit and use targeted mutation, fault injection, or compensating evidence.

ballot_rationales.rationale: A recurrence guard that demonstrates only nearby correct behavior does not prove the defect's causal trigger is blocked. Reproducing that trigger, including consequential negative behavior, is the professionally necessary link between the regression mechanism and the claimed fix.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies when a causal trigger can be identified for regression testing; if it cannot be exercised in the available environment, that proof limit and residual recurrence risk remain explicit.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: When the trigger cannot be reproduced, record the proof limit and retain residual recurrence risk.

ballot_rationales.rationale: A regression guard proves recurrence prevention only when it reproduces the causal trigger instead of merely testing adjacent correct behavior.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies only after an accepted defect, incident, review finding, or equivalent recurrence mechanism is known.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Keep the causal-trigger rule front-loaded and require explicit proof limits when safe reproduction is infeasible.

ballot_rationales.rationale: A single task needs no DAG, and every retained edge must represent a real blocking fact so scheduling, critical-path, and parallel-safety claims remain executable rather than ceremonial.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: The planner operates from an accepted Engineering Brief when at least two real tasks have evidenced dependency or parallel, integration, migration, or release value.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Return the unchanged Brief slice when a DAG is unnecessary and block unknown or unsupported edges instead of creating placeholders.

ballot_rationales.rationale: A DAG adds value only when at least two real tasks have dependency structure, and every edge must represent an actual blocking fact. The threshold prevents ceremonial planning while the edge rule prevents false sequencing and hidden parallelism constraints.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies after an accepted Brief identifies two or more real tasks; one task remains a direct Task Contract, and independent tasks need no invented blocking edge.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Reject single-task DAGs and any edge lacking a source-backed blocking dependency.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The two-task threshold avoids ceremonial DAGs, while requiring every actual edge to represent a blocking fact preserves graph semantics.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies when an accepted Brief contains at least two real tasks with evidenced dependency, parallel, integration, or release-order value.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Keep zero-edge parallel DAGs permissible and reject invented nodes, edges, cycles, or placeholder work.

ballot_rationales.rationale: A specialist supplies bounded risk expertise but does not own complete changed-scope coverage, so allowing it to replace final implementation review would leave unassigned professional-risk dimensions and diff paths.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: The ai-code-review-refactor contract delegates specialists only for concrete named risk while retaining one accountable final review owner.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Merge specialist findings into the primary review and require the final reviewer to inspect the latest actual diff and every changed file.

ballot_rationales.rationale: A specialist decides its named risk dimension but does not inspect or bind the entire latest implementation diff. Requiring final implementation review preserves complete changed-file coverage, acceptance mapping, validation freshness, unnecessary scope checks, and a single overall verdict.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies whenever specialist review is triggered; its evidence supplements but cannot replace the independently assigned final implementation review of the latest diff and every changed file.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Require a final latest-diff review after specialist evidence and repeat it after every material repair.

ballot_rationales.rationale: A risk-specific Specialist covers only its named lens, so it cannot substitute for the independent final review of the whole changed scope.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies whenever implementation review delegates a concrete risk dimension to a Specialist Skill.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Keep the review owner responsible for merging Specialist findings into the complete final implementation review.

limitations: This majority is authoring lifecycle evidence only.
It cannot satisfy readability or professional-completeness formal attestations.
The record contains no generated single-source-of-truth disposition entries.
A rewrite majority requires a source edit before any resolved governance entry can exist.
